Frequently Asked Questions
Which meeting apps allow free recording in 2026?
Three apps allow free meeting recording without a monthly minute cap in 2026: (1) Meetily Community Edition - free, open source under MIT, records and transcribes locally on Windows and macOS with no monthly caps; (2) Fathom Free - unlimited cloud recordings, transcripts and storage (advanced AI summaries on the first 5 calls each month); (3) OBS Studio - free, open source under GPLv2, records anything on screen but requires audio-routing setup and has no transcription. Capped free tiers, checked October 11, 2026: Otter Basic (300 minutes/month, 30 minutes per conversation, 3 lifetime imports), Fireflies Free (400 minutes of storage per seat, 20 one-time AI credits), Granola Free (30 days of meeting history), tl;dv Free (unlimited recordings, but full AI notes only for your first 10 meetings and 5 file uploads, for the life of the account), Loom Starter (25 videos, 5-minute recordings). Zoom's free plan records locally and adds 3 AI summaries a month through ZoomMate Basic.
How do I record a meeting for free?
On Windows or macOS, the fastest free path is: (1) Install Meetily Community Edition (free, open source) from meetily.ai; (2) Pick the Whisper or Parakeet transcription engine in setup; (3) Start the recording before joining your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call. Meetily captures system audio and microphone locally without joining the meeting as a bot, so other participants see no notetaker bot. The recording and transcript stay on your machine, and summaries use a local model or your own API key. If you want a cloud option, Fathom Free records in the cloud and joins as a visible bot unless you use its Mac-only bot-free mode. Our guide on how to record a meeting covers each platform step by step, including consent.
What's the best free meeting recorder AND transcriber?
For free recording plus AI transcription in one app, Meetily Community Edition is the strongest pick if you want audio kept on your device: it captures system audio locally (no bot in the call), transcribes with OpenAI Whisper or Parakeet across 99+ languages, and stores everything on-device under the MIT license. Fathom Free is the strongest cloud alternative - unlimited transcription, but audio is processed in Fathom's cloud and its bot-free mode is Mac-only. OBS Studio records audio but does not transcribe. Of the ten tools in this guide, Meetily, OBS Studio and Zoom's local recording keep the recording file on your device, and only Meetily adds on-device transcription. OpenWhispr and Anarlog are other open-source local options outside the ranked list.
What recording devices work best for in-person meetings?
For in-person meetings, the recording stack splits into hardware and software. Hardware: a dedicated USB conference mic (Jabra Speak 750, Anker PowerConf S330, or a Blue Yeti) placed centrally on the table captures all speakers cleanly. Phone-based options like an iPhone laid flat work in a pinch. Software: route the mic into a local recorder like Meetily on a laptop and let Whisper transcribe in real time. Meetily works the same way for in-person as for online meetings because it captures whatever audio your system hears. Bot-based cloud tools cannot record an in-person room by joining a call; some offer a separate mobile or desktop app for that, which sends the audio to the vendor's cloud.
Best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026?
The best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026 depends on whether you need the data to stay local. Best local-first: Meetily - free Community Edition under MIT, no bot, Whisper or Parakeet transcription, works offline. Best cloud free plan: Fathom - unlimited recordings and transcripts, with advanced AI summaries on five calls a month. Best for sales teams: Fireflies.ai with Salesforce/HubSpot CRM sync ($10/user/month billed annually on Pro). Best for Microsoft 365 shops: Microsoft 365 Copilot, an add-on license on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan. Best raw recorder without transcription: OBS Studio.
What's the best meeting recording app?
The best meeting recording app for people who want recordings to stay private in 2026 is Meetily: it records Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and Webex calls locally on Windows or macOS (Apple Silicon), adds no bot to the meeting, and the Community Edition is free under the MIT license. It bundles AI transcription (Whisper or Parakeet) and AI summaries in the same app, so you do not need a separate transcriber. For sales-heavy workflows with CRM dependency, Fireflies.ai is the conventional pick. For unlimited free cloud recording, Fathom is the alternative. None of the other apps in this guide combine bot-free, local, and free in one package.
What app should I use to record meetings?
Match the app to the constraint. Privacy or compliance constraint (healthcare, legal, financial, regulated industries): Meetily Community Edition - local recording, no audio upload, MIT-licensed. Cost constraint with unlimited free needed: Meetily or Fathom Free. Workflow constraint (CRM sync, sales coaching): Fireflies.ai. Microsoft 365 constraint: Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Teams. Polished notes app: Granola (captures audio on your device without a bot but processes notes in the cloud; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and Business is $14/user/month). For most people who want privacy, low cost, and no bot together, Meetily covers all three.
Top meeting recording tools in 2026?
Our ranked top 10 meeting recording tools for 2026, ordered by the criteria in this guide (where audio is stored first, then bot use and free-tier limits), with primary trade-offs: (1) Meetily - local, no bot, Community Edition free under MIT; (2) Fathom Free - cloud, unlimited free recordings and transcription, bot by default (bot-free on Mac); (3) OBS Studio - powerful local recorder, no transcription, steep setup; (4) Otter.ai - cloud, capped free tier, bot or desktop app, subject of a pending privacy class action; (5) Fireflies.ai - cloud, CRM-friendly, capped free tier, a pending BIPA lawsuit; (6) tl;dv - cloud, free recordings but lifetime-capped AI notes, multi-meeting AI reports; (7) Zoom local recording - Zoom-only, ZoomMate Basic adds 3 summaries a month; (8) Google Meet recording - needs Workspace Business Standard or higher; (9) Microsoft Teams recording - needs a paid Microsoft 365 plan; (10) Loom - async video, free Starter plan limited to 25 videos.
Is Meetily really free?
Yes. Meetily's Community Edition is free and open source under the MIT license, with no monthly minute or meeting caps. It includes core features like real-time transcription, AI summaries, and local recording. Pro features like speaker identification, auto-detect meetings, and advanced exports are available at $10/user/month billed annually. The core recorder is free.
Does Meetily work with Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet?
Yes, Meetily records any meeting platform because it captures your system audio and microphone. It's platform-agnostic and works with Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Discord, Slack Huddles, Webex, and any other platform that outputs audio through your computer.
Can other meeting participants see Meetily recording?
No bot appears in the call. Meetily is bot-free, which means it doesn't add any visible participant to your meetings. Fireflies, Otter.ai, Fathom and tl;dv join as a visible Notetaker bot by default (each also has a desktop mode that records without one), while Meetily captures audio locally. Only you see that it is recording. You should still follow proper consent laws and inform participants when recording.
Where are my recordings stored?
All recordings are stored locally on your computer in a folder you choose. Audio is never uploaded to a cloud service. You can back the files up, encrypt them, or delete them anytime. If you use your own API key for summaries, the transcript text is sent to the provider you chose; a local summary model keeps summaries on your device too. This fits GDPR, HIPAA, and other compliance requirements by design, but confirm your own obligations with your compliance team.
Does Meetily require internet to work?
No. Once installed and with AI models downloaded, recording and transcription work completely offline. The AI transcription runs on your local machine using Whisper or Parakeet engines. Only the initial download requires internet, and summaries stay offline only with a local model (an API key needs a connection). This suits air-gapped environments and unreliable connections.
How accurate is Meetily's transcription?
Meetily uses OpenAI's Whisper model, which delivers high accuracy on clear audio in English, and supports 99+ languages. The Large v3 model provides the best accuracy, while smaller models (Base, Small) offer faster performance on older hardware.
What are the system requirements for Meetily?
Minimum: a Windows PC or an Apple Silicon Mac with 8GB RAM, a 4-core CPU, and 10GB storage. Recommended: 16GB RAM, an 8-core CPU, 50GB storage, GPU acceleration (NVIDIA, AMD, or Apple Silicon), and an SSD. The Whisper Tiny model works on older hardware, while larger models benefit from newer systems.
Is Meetily GDPR and HIPAA compliant?
By design, not by certification. Transcription runs on your device, so audio is not sent to a third party, which helps with EU data residency and HIPAA requirements. If you choose your own API key for summaries, that provider receives the transcript text and belongs in your compliance review; a local summary model avoids this. Meetily does not hold formal GDPR or HIPAA certifications, and the open-source code allows security audits. Check your own obligations with your compliance team.
How can I record a meeting without using Zoom's built-in recorder?
Use a standalone meeting recorder like Meetily that captures your system audio directly. Install it on your computer, start the recording before your Zoom call, and it will capture everything without using Zoom's native recording. This means no recording notification is sent to participants (though you should still inform them per consent laws), and your recording stays on your local device instead of Zoom's cloud servers.
Which meeting recorders work for both in-person and online meetings?
Meetily and OBS Studio both work for in-person meetings because they capture audio from your device's microphone. For in-person meetings, place your laptop in the room and Meetily will record and transcribe using its AI engine. For online meetings, it captures system audio. Cloud tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies join online meetings with a bot by default and offer separate desktop or mobile apps for other situations; their audio goes to the vendor's cloud.
Are there meeting recorders that don't store audio in the cloud?
Yes. Meetily stores everything locally on your computer with no audio uploads. OBS Studio also records locally. Zoom offers local recording (not cloud) on its free tier. All other tools in this list - Fathom, Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and tl;dv - upload your meeting audio to cloud servers for processing, including in their bot-free desktop modes.

Why Do Most Meeting Recorders Fall Short?

Before we dive into the options, let's address the elephant in the room. Most meeting recording tools in 2026 fall into one of four traps:

Too complex - Like OBS Studio, which requires configuring virtual audio cables and scene management
Cloud-only audio - Tools that upload your meeting audio to the vendor's servers
Bot-dependent - Tools that join the call as a visible "Notetaker" participant by default. Many now offer a desktop app that records without one, so check which mode the free plan includes
Tight free tiers - Otter's free plan is 300 minutes a month with 30-minute conversations and 3 lifetime imports, and tl;dv's AI notes on the free plan cover only your first 10 meetings

What Makes Good Meeting Recorder Software?

The ideal meeting recording software in 2026 should be simple to set up, work without internet, keep your data local, and never require a visible bot in your meetings. Only a few tools meet all four criteria.

Why Does Privacy Matter for Meeting Recording?

When you record a meeting, you capture potentially sensitive information:

Business strategies and plans
Client conversations and deal terms
Employee performance discussions
Financial data and projections
Personal details shared in conversation

Cloud-based meeting recording tools store all of this on their servers. Even with encryption, you are trusting a third party with your most sensitive conversations. Model-training policies differ by vendor, so read them. Granola's security page
(opens in new tab)
 says it trains on anonymized data and that you can opt out in Settings, with training off by default for Enterprise workspaces. tl;dv's privacy policy
(opens in new tab)
 says customer content is not used to train AI models.

The risk is not theoretical. In August 2025, a federal class action lawsuit was filed against Otter.ai
(opens in new tab)
 (Brewer v. Otter.ai, N.D. Cal., reported by NPR, August 2025) alleging the bot records meetings and trains on transcripts without all-party consent. In December 2025, Fireflies.ai was sued under Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act
(opens in new tab)
 (National Law Review, December 2025) for collecting voiceprints without explicit consent. A local-first recorder like Meetily takes the vendor out of the audio path, because audio and transcription stay on the host's device. Summaries stay local with a local model, or go to the API provider you choose.

Pricing economics push the same way. Cloud speech APIs such as AWS Transcribe
(opens in new tab)
 and Google Cloud Speech-to-Text
(opens in new tab)
 bill per audio minute, and cloud meeting-AI products add their own per-seat plans on top. Self-hosted transcription with OpenAI's open-source Whisper model
(opens in new tab)
 (released under the MIT license in September 2022 by OpenAI) has no per-minute fee.

GDPR and Compliance Warning

For European businesses, sending meeting recordings to a cloud vendor can raise GDPR questions about where the data is processed and under which terms. Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and Fathom process meeting audio in the cloud, so review each vendor's data-processing terms and hosting options. Local recording with a tool like Meetily keeps the audio on your own device. See our GDPR compliance guide for more details.

How Do I Choose the Right Meeting Recorder Software?

Ask yourself these questions:

Do you need offline capability?

If you travel, work in areas with unreliable internet, or need to record in air-gapped environments, choose Meetily or OBS. All cloud-based tools (Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, tl;dv) require a stable internet connection.

How important is privacy?

If you are recording sensitive business conversations, healthcare discussions, legal meetings, or financial reviews, local-first AI meeting recording tools like Meetily fit best. No cloud provider can leak audio that never left your device.

Do you need a recording bot to be invisible?

If you record client calls, sales demos, or any meeting where a visible "Notetaker" bot would be awkward or unprofessional, choose a tool that captures audio on your own device: Meetily (local, open source) or Granola (cloud processing; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and paid plans start at $14/user/month). Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, and tl;dv join as a visible bot by default; each also has a desktop mode without one (Fathom's is Mac-only), so check that the mode is available on your plan and platform.

Do you need CRM integration?

If your workflow requires meeting notes to automatically sync to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive, Fireflies.ai is the strongest option. Meetily has no native CRM integrations; with Meetily Pro, your own script can send notes to a CRM through its webhooks and command-line tool.

Do you need transcription?

If you want searchable, text-based records of your meetings, choose a tool with AI transcription (Meetily, Fathom, Otter, Fireflies, or tl;dv) over basic screen recording (OBS, Loom).

How tech-savvy are you?

OBS requires significant technical knowledge. Every other tool on this list is designed for quick setup, with Meetily and cloud tools ready to record in under 5 minutes.

Our ranked top 10 meeting recording tools for 2026, ordered by the criteria in this guide (where audio is stored first, then bot use and free-tier limits), with primary trade-offs: (1) Meetily - local, no bot, Community Edition free under MIT; (2) Fathom Free - cloud, unlimited free recordings and transcription, bot by default (bot-free on Mac); (3) OBS Studio - powerful local recorder, no transcription, steep setup; (4) Otter.ai - cloud, capped free tier, bot or desktop app, subject of a pending privacy class action; (5) Fireflies.ai - cloud, CRM-friendly, capped free tier, a pending BIPA lawsuit; (6) tl;dv - cloud, free recordings but lifetime-capped AI notes, multi-meeting AI reports; (7) Zoom local recording - Zoom-only, ZoomMate Basic adds 3 summaries a month; (8) Google Meet recording - needs Workspace Business Standard or higher; (9) Microsoft Teams recording - needs a paid Microsoft 365 plan; (10) Loom - async video, free Starter plan limited to 25 videos.
Is Meetily really free?
Yes. Meetily's Community Edition is free and open source under the MIT license, with no monthly minute or meeting caps. It includes core features like real-time transcription, AI summaries, and local recording. Pro features like speaker identification, auto-detect meetings, and advanced exports are available at $10/user/month billed annually. The core recorder is free.
Does Meetily work with Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet?
Yes, Meetily records any meeting platform because it captures your system audio and microphone. It's platform-agnostic and works with Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Discord, Slack Huddles, Webex, and any other platform that outputs audio through your computer.
Can other meeting participants see Meetily recording?
No bot appears in the call. Meetily is bot-free, which means it doesn't add any visible participant to your meetings. Fireflies, Otter.ai, Fathom and tl;dv join as a visible Notetaker bot by default (each also has a desktop mode that records without one), while Meetily captures audio locally. Only you see that it is recording. You should still follow proper consent laws and inform participants when recording.
Where are my recordings stored?
All recordings are stored locally on your computer in a folder you choose. Audio is never uploaded to a cloud service. You can back the files up, encrypt them, or delete them anytime. If you use your own API key for summaries, the transcript text is sent to the provider you chose; a local summary model keeps summaries on your device too. This fits GDPR, HIPAA, and other compliance requirements by design, but confirm your own obligations with your compliance team.
Does Meetily require internet to work?
No. Once installed and with AI models downloaded, recording and transcription work completely offline. The AI transcription runs on your local machine using Whisper or Parakeet engines. Only the initial download requires internet, and summaries stay offline only with a local model (an API key needs a connection). This suits air-gapped environments and unreliable connections.
How accurate is Meetily's transcription?
Meetily uses OpenAI's Whisper model, which delivers high accuracy on clear audio in English, and supports 99+ languages. The Large v3 model provides the best accuracy, while smaller models (Base, Small) offer faster performance on older hardware.
What are the system requirements for Meetily?
Minimum: a Windows PC or an Apple Silicon Mac with 8GB RAM, a 4-core CPU, and 10GB storage. Recommended: 16GB RAM, an 8-core CPU, 50GB storage, GPU acceleration (NVIDIA, AMD, or Apple Silicon), and an SSD. The Whisper Tiny model works on older hardware, while larger models benefit from newer systems.
Is Meetily GDPR and HIPAA compliant?
By design, not by certification. Transcription runs on your device, so audio is not sent to a third party, which helps with EU data residency and HIPAA requirements. If you choose your own API key for summaries, that provider receives the transcript text and belongs in your compliance review; a local summary model avoids this. Meetily does not hold formal GDPR or HIPAA certifications, and the open-source code allows security audits. Check your own obligations with your compliance team.
How can I record a meeting without using Zoom's built-in recorder?
Use a standalone meeting recorder like Meetily that captures your system audio directly. Install it on your computer, start the recording before your Zoom call, and it will capture everything without using Zoom's native recording. This means no recording notification is sent to participants (though you should still inform them per consent laws), and your recording stays on your local device instead of Zoom's cloud servers.
Which meeting recorders work for both in-person and online meetings?
Meetily and OBS Studio both work for in-person meetings because they capture audio from your device's microphone. For in-person meetings, place your laptop in the room and Meetily will record and transcribe using its AI engine. For online meetings, it captures system audio. Cloud tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies join online meetings with a bot by default and offer separate desktop or mobile apps for other situations; their audio goes to the vendor's cloud.
Are there meeting recorders that don't store audio in the cloud?
Yes. Meetily stores everything locally on your computer with no audio uploads. OBS Studio also records locally. Zoom offers local recording (not cloud) on its free tier. All other tools in this list - Fathom, Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and tl;dv - upload your meeting audio to cloud servers for processing, including in their bot-free desktop modes.

Meetily is our product. It is listed first because it fits the criteria below, and we say where another tool is the better fit.

children.text: Best Free AI Meeting Recording Software and AI Voice Recorders

If you specifically need AI-powered meeting recording software with transcription and summarization, your options narrow. Not every meeting recorder includes AI features, and the quality varies widely.

AI meeting recording tools use speech-to-text models to automatically transcribe your meetings, identify speakers, and generate summaries with action items. The best AI voice recorders for meetings in 2026 combine accurate transcription with useful post-meeting intelligence.
If you want help across all your meetings rather than one recording at a time, see how Meetily works as an AI meeting assistant. If notes are all you need, the AI note taker page is the shorter read.
Here is how the AI meeting recording software options compare:

Meetily uses OpenAI Whisper and NVIDIA Parakeet models locally, delivering high transcription accuracy on clear English audio. Because transcription runs on your device, meeting audio is not sent to any server. That architecture supports GDPR and HIPAA compliance by design; summaries stay on-device with a local model, or go to the API provider you choose.
Fathom provides cloud-based AI summaries with highlights and video clips. The free plan has unlimited transcription and advanced AI summaries on the first 5 calls each month.
Otter.ai is known for real-time AI transcription during meetings, and transcribes in six languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese.
Fireflies.ai adds conversation intelligence and sentiment analysis on top of transcription, a feature-rich option for sales teams. It supports 100+ languages.
tl;dv offers multi-meeting AI reports that analyze patterns across your calls, useful for sales coaching and team reviews. It supports 30+ languages.

OBS Studio does not include AI transcription. The platform-native recorders now add AI notes only through limited free allowances (Zoom's ZoomMate Basic) or paid plans (Google Meet, Teams); see their entries above. If AI transcription is a requirement, choose Meetily or one of the cloud tools listed above.
Why Does Privacy Matter for Meeting Recording?
When you record a meeting, you capture potentially sensitive information:

Cloud-based meeting recording tools store all of this on their servers. Even with encryption, you are trusting a third party with your most sensitive conversations. Model-training policies differ by vendor, so read them. Granola's security page
(opens in new tab)
 says it trains on anonymized data and that you can opt out in Settings, with training off by default for Enterprise workspaces. tl;dv's privacy policy
(opens in new tab)
 says customer content is not used to train AI models.

The risk is not theoretical. In August 2025, a federal class action lawsuit was filed against Otter.ai
(opens in new tab)
 (Brewer v. Otter.ai, N.D. Cal., reported by NPR, August 2025) alleging the bot records meetings and trains on transcripts without all-party consent. In December 2025, Fireflies.ai was sued under Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act
(opens in new tab)
 (National Law Review, December 2025) for collecting voiceprints without explicit consent. A local-first recorder like Meetily takes the vendor out of the audio path, because audio and transcription stay on the host's device. Summaries stay local with a local model, or go to the API provider you choose.

Pricing economics push the same way. Cloud speech APIs such as AWS Transcribe
(opens in new tab)
 and Google Cloud Speech-to-Text
(opens in new tab)
 bill per audio minute, and cloud meeting-AI products add their own per-seat plans on top. Self-hosted transcription with OpenAI's open-source Whisper model
(opens in new tab)
 (released under the MIT license in September 2022 by OpenAI) has no per-minute fee.

For European businesses, sending meeting recordings to a cloud vendor can raise GDPR questions about where the data is processed and under which terms. Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and Fathom process meeting audio in the cloud, so review each vendor's data-processing terms and hosting options. Local recording with a tool like Meetily keeps the audio on your own device. See our GDPR compliance guide for more details.
Why Is "OBS Alternative for Meetings" a Top Search?
OBS Studio is powerful, but it wasn't designed as meeting recording software. Here's why people search for OBS alternatives:
Complex setup - Virtual audio routing requires configuring tools like VB-Cable or BlackHole
No transcription - OBS records video and audio, not text
Overkill features - Most users need 5% of what OBS offers
No meeting-specific features - No speaker identification, action items, or AI summaries
Meetily is essentially "OBS for meetings" - all the local, private recording benefits without the complexity, plus AI transcription built in.
How Do I Choose the Right Meeting Recorder Software?

If you travel, work in areas with unreliable internet, or need to record in air-gapped environments, choose Meetily or OBS. All cloud-based tools (Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, tl;dv) require a stable internet connection.

If you are recording sensitive business conversations, healthcare discussions, legal meetings, or financial reviews, local-first AI meeting recording tools like Meetily fit best. No cloud provider can leak audio that never left your device.
Do you need a recording bot to be invisible?

If you record client calls, sales demos, or any meeting where a visible "Notetaker" bot would be awkward or unprofessional, choose a tool that captures audio on your own device: Meetily (local, open source) or Granola (cloud processing; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and paid plans start at $14/user/month). Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, and tl;dv join as a visible bot by default; each also has a desktop mode without one (Fathom's is Mac-only), so check that the mode is available on your plan and platform.

If your workflow requires meeting notes to automatically sync to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive, Fireflies.ai is the strongest option. Meetily has no native CRM integrations; with Meetily Pro, your own script can send notes to a CRM through its webhooks and command-line tool.
If you want searchable, text-based records of your meetings, choose a tool with AI transcription (Meetily, Fathom, Otter, Fireflies, or tl;dv) over basic screen recording (OBS, Loom).
OBS requires significant technical knowledge. Every other tool on this list is designed for quick setup, with Meetily and cloud tools ready to record in under 5 minutes.
How Do I Get Started with Meetily?

Install the application on your computer
Choose your transcription engine (Whisper for accuracy, Parakeet for speed)

The Community Edition needs no account, never uploads your audio, and adds no bot to the call. For the full walkthrough on Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, including the consent steps to follow before you hit record, see our guide on how to record a meeting.

The best free meeting recorder software in 2026 isn't the one with the most features - it's the one that fits how you actually work.

If none of these fits, try Meetily and see whether recording on your own device suits how you work.

children.a: Three apps allow free meeting recording without a monthly minute cap in 2026: (1) Meetily Community Edition - free, open source under MIT, records and transcribes locally on Windows and macOS with no monthly caps; (2) Fathom Free - unlimited cloud recordings, transcripts and storage (advanced AI summaries on the first 5 calls each month); (3) OBS Studio - free, open source under GPLv2, records anything on screen but requires audio-routing setup and has no transcription. Capped free tiers, checked October 11, 2026: Otter Basic (300 minutes/month, 30 minutes per conversation, 3 lifetime imports), Fireflies Free (400 minutes of storage per seat, 20 one-time AI credits), Granola Free (30 days of meeting history), tl;dv Free (unlimited recordings, but full AI notes only for your first 10 meetings and 5 file uploads, for the life of the account), Loom Starter (25 videos, 5-minute recordings). Zoom's free plan records locally and adds 3 AI summaries a month through ZoomMate Basic.

children.q: How do I record a meeting for free?
children.a: On Windows or macOS, the fastest free path is: (1) Install Meetily Community Edition (free, open source) from meetily.ai; (2) Pick the Whisper or Parakeet transcription engine in setup; (3) Start the recording before joining your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call. Meetily captures system audio and microphone locally without joining the meeting as a bot, so other participants see no notetaker bot. The recording and transcript stay on your machine, and summaries use a local model or your own API key. If you want a cloud option, Fathom Free records in the cloud and joins as a visible bot unless you use its Mac-only bot-free mode. Our guide on how to record a meeting covers each platform step by step, including consent.

children.q: What's the best free meeting recorder AND transcriber?
children.a: For free recording plus AI transcription in one app, Meetily Community Edition is the strongest pick if you want audio kept on your device: it captures system audio locally (no bot in the call), transcribes with OpenAI Whisper or Parakeet across 99+ languages, and stores everything on-device under the MIT license. Fathom Free is the strongest cloud alternative - unlimited transcription, but audio is processed in Fathom's cloud and its bot-free mode is Mac-only. OBS Studio records audio but does not transcribe. Of the ten tools in this guide, Meetily, OBS Studio and Zoom's local recording keep the recording file on your device, and only Meetily adds on-device transcription. OpenWhispr and Anarlog are other open-source local options outside the ranked list.

children.q: What recording devices work best for in-person meetings?
children.a: For in-person meetings, the recording stack splits into hardware and software. Hardware: a dedicated USB conference mic (Jabra Speak 750, Anker PowerConf S330, or a Blue Yeti) placed centrally on the table captures all speakers cleanly. Phone-based options like an iPhone laid flat work in a pinch. Software: route the mic into a local recorder like Meetily on a laptop and let Whisper transcribe in real time. Meetily works the same way for in-person as for online meetings because it captures whatever audio your system hears. Bot-based cloud tools cannot record an in-person room by joining a call; some offer a separate mobile or desktop app for that, which sends the audio to the vendor's cloud.

children.q: Best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026?
children.a: The best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026 depends on whether you need the data to stay local. Best local-first: Meetily - free Community Edition under MIT, no bot, Whisper or Parakeet transcription, works offline. Best cloud free plan: Fathom - unlimited recordings and transcripts, with advanced AI summaries on five calls a month. Best for sales teams: Fireflies.ai with Salesforce/HubSpot CRM sync ($10/user/month billed annually on Pro). Best for Microsoft 365 shops: Microsoft 365 Copilot, an add-on license on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan. Best raw recorder without transcription: OBS Studio.

children.q: What's the best meeting recording app?
children.a: The best meeting recording app for people who want recordings to stay private in 2026 is Meetily: it records Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and Webex calls locally on Windows or macOS (Apple Silicon), adds no bot to the meeting, and the Community Edition is free under the MIT license. It bundles AI transcription (Whisper or Parakeet) and AI summaries in the same app, so you do not need a separate transcriber. For sales-heavy workflows with CRM dependency, Fireflies.ai is the conventional pick. For unlimited free cloud recording, Fathom is the alternative. None of the other apps in this guide combine bot-free, local, and free in one package.

children.q: What app should I use to record meetings?
children.a: Match the app to the constraint. Privacy or compliance constraint (healthcare, legal, financial, regulated industries): Meetily Community Edition - local recording, no audio upload, MIT-licensed. Cost constraint with unlimited free needed: Meetily or Fathom Free. Workflow constraint (CRM sync, sales coaching): Fireflies.ai. Microsoft 365 constraint: Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Teams. Polished notes app: Granola (captures audio on your device without a bot but processes notes in the cloud; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and Business is $14/user/month). For most people who want privacy, low cost, and no bot together, Meetily covers all three.

children.q: Top meeting recording tools in 2026?
children.a: Our ranked top 10 meeting recording tools for 2026, ordered by the criteria in this guide (where audio is stored first, then bot use and free-tier limits), with primary trade-offs: (1) Meetily - local, no bot, Community Edition free under MIT; (2) Fathom Free - cloud, unlimited free recordings and transcription, bot by default (bot-free on Mac); (3) OBS Studio - powerful local recorder, no transcription, steep setup; (4) Otter.ai - cloud, capped free tier, bot or desktop app, subject of a pending privacy class action; (5) Fireflies.ai - cloud, CRM-friendly, capped free tier, a pending BIPA lawsuit; (6) tl;dv - cloud, free recordings but lifetime-capped AI notes, multi-meeting AI reports; (7) Zoom local recording - Zoom-only, ZoomMate Basic adds 3 summaries a month; (8) Google Meet recording - needs Workspace Business Standard or higher; (9) Microsoft Teams recording - needs a paid Microsoft 365 plan; (10) Loom - async video, free Starter plan limited to 25 videos.

children.q: Is Meetily really free?
children.a: Yes. Meetily's Community Edition is free and open source under the MIT license, with no monthly minute or meeting caps. It includes core features like real-time transcription, AI summaries, and local recording. Pro features like speaker identification, auto-detect meetings, and advanced exports are available at $10/user/month billed annually. The core recorder is free.

children.q: Does Meetily work with Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet?
children.a: Yes, Meetily records any meeting platform because it captures your system audio and microphone. It's platform-agnostic and works with Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Discord, Slack Huddles, Webex, and any other platform that outputs audio through your computer.

children.q: Can other meeting participants see Meetily recording?
children.a: No bot appears in the call. Meetily is bot-free, which means it doesn't add any visible participant to your meetings. Fireflies, Otter.ai, Fathom and tl;dv join as a visible Notetaker bot by default (each also has a desktop mode that records without one), while Meetily captures audio locally. Only you see that it is recording. You should still follow proper consent laws and inform participants when recording.

children.q: Where are my recordings stored?
children.a: All recordings are stored locally on your computer in a folder you choose. Audio is never uploaded to a cloud service. You can back the files up, encrypt them, or delete them anytime. If you use your own API key for summaries, the transcript text is sent to the provider you chose; a local summary model keeps summaries on your device too. This fits GDPR, HIPAA, and other compliance requirements by design, but confirm your own obligations with your compliance team.

children.q: Does Meetily require internet to work?
children.a: No. Once installed and with AI models downloaded, recording and transcription work completely offline. The AI transcription runs on your local machine using Whisper or Parakeet engines. Only the initial download requires internet, and summaries stay offline only with a local model (an API key needs a connection). This suits air-gapped environments and unreliable connections.

children.q: How accurate is Meetily's transcription?
children.a: Meetily uses OpenAI's Whisper model, which delivers high accuracy on clear audio in English, and supports 99+ languages. The Large v3 model provides the best accuracy, while smaller models (Base, Small) offer faster performance on older hardware.

children.q: What are the system requirements for Meetily?
children.a: Minimum: a Windows PC or an Apple Silicon Mac with 8GB RAM, a 4-core CPU, and 10GB storage. Recommended: 16GB RAM, an 8-core CPU, 50GB storage, GPU acceleration (NVIDIA, AMD, or Apple Silicon), and an SSD. The Whisper Tiny model works on older hardware, while larger models benefit from newer systems.

children.q: Is Meetily GDPR and HIPAA compliant?
children.a: By design, not by certification. Transcription runs on your device, so audio is not sent to a third party, which helps with EU data residency and HIPAA requirements. If you choose your own API key for summaries, that provider receives the transcript text and belongs in your compliance review; a local summary model avoids this. Meetily does not hold formal GDPR or HIPAA certifications, and the open-source code allows security audits. Check your own obligations with your compliance team.

children.q: How can I record a meeting without using Zoom's built-in recorder?
children.a: Use a standalone meeting recorder like Meetily that captures your system audio directly. Install it on your computer, start the recording before your Zoom call, and it will capture everything without using Zoom's native recording. This means no recording notification is sent to participants (though you should still inform them per consent laws), and your recording stays on your local device instead of Zoom's cloud servers.

children.q: Which meeting recorders work for both in-person and online meetings?
children.a: Meetily and OBS Studio both work for in-person meetings because they capture audio from your device's microphone. For in-person meetings, place your laptop in the room and Meetily will record and transcribe using its AI engine. For online meetings, it captures system audio. Cloud tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies join online meetings with a bot by default and offer separate desktop or mobile apps for other situations; their audio goes to the vendor's cloud.

children.q: Are there meeting recorders that don't store audio in the cloud?
children.a: Yes. Meetily stores everything locally on your computer with no audio uploads. OBS Studio also records locally. Zoom offers local recording (not cloud) on its free tier. All other tools in this list - Fathom, Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and tl;dv - upload your meeting audio to cloud servers for processing, including in their bot-free desktop modes.

Introduction: The Bot-Free Revolution

If you've used Fireflies.ai, you've experienced this:

"Fireflies Notetaker has joined the meeting"

That moment when your client sees the recording bot. The awkward pause. The "are we being recorded?" question. The scramble to explain your AI note-taking tool.

What if the bot simply didn't exist?

That's the promise of bot-free meeting transcription. Meetily captures your meetings invisibly-no bots, no announcements, no disruption-while giving you the same AI-powered transcription and summaries.

But there's a tradeoff: Fireflies is plug-and-play cloud convenience. Meetily requires local installation and processing. Which is right for you?

This comprehensive comparison answers that question.

• Choose Meetily if you prioritize privacy, bot-free recording, local processing, or work in regulated industries (HIPAA, GDPR)

Privacy & Data Security: The #1 Differentiator

This is where the philosophical difference between the two tools becomes stark.

Fireflies.ai: Cloud-Based Processing

How it works:

Fireflies bot joins your meeting
Audio is streamed to Fireflies servers
Transcription happens on Fireflies infrastructure (AWS)
Transcript and audio are stored on Fireflies cloud
You access via Fireflies web app

Privacy Concerns:

Third-party processor: Your meeting data is handled by Fireflies
HIPAA Compliance: Only available for Enterprise plan customers ($39/user/month) with signed BAA-not available for Free, Pro, or Business plans
Cloud storage: Audio recordings and transcripts live on Fireflies servers
US jurisdiction: Data subject to US laws (CLOUD Act, etc.)
Data access: Fireflies employees have technical access to your data
Meetily: Local-First Privacy

How it works:

You start recording on your device (Community Edition: manual start, Pro: automatic detection)
Audio is captured from your system (never uploaded)
Transcription happens on YOUR computer (Whisper or Parakeet engine)
Transcript is saved to YOUR local storage
Optional: Use local LLM (Ollama) or bring your own API key for summaries

Privacy Benefits:

Local transcription: Audio and transcripts stay on your device
Pluggable AI summaries: Choose local models or your own API key
GDPR compliant by design: Transcription runs locally, you control your summary provider
HIPAA compliant by design: Use fully local processing for regulated data
No data mining: Open-source code means no hidden telemetry

Who Wins?

• Fireflies: If you trust cloud providers, want zero setup, and work in unregulated industries
• Meetily: If you work in healthcare, legal, finance, government, or anywhere data sovereignty matters

Bot Visibility: Invisible Recording vs Visible Bots
Fireflies.ai: The Visible Bot

When you use Fireflies, it joins your meeting as a participant:

Appears in participant list as "Fireflies Notetaker" or similar
Shows video thumbnail (usually Fireflies logo)
Announces "Fireflies has joined the meeting" (on some platforms)
Can be seen by all participants
Meetily: Invisible Recording

Meetily captures your computer's system audio:

No bot joins the meeting (other participants see only you)
Invisible to all meeting participants
No participant list entry, no video thumbnail
Platform-agnostic (works with ANY meeting software)

The Tradeoff: Automation vs Invisibility

Fireflies offers automatic meeting joining: Schedule Fireflies to auto-join your calendar meetings without you clicking anything.

Meetily offers two options:

• Pro: Automatically detects and records meetings (similar automation to Fireflies, but invisible)
• Community Edition: Manual start/stop recording (use keyboard shortcuts for convenience)

Scenario 1: Healthcare Practice

Dr. Smith runs a 10-physician medical practice. They conduct 500+ patient consultations per month via telehealth.

With Fireflies:
❌ Bot joining patient calls creates discomfort

Written by the Meetily team. We built Meetily after seeing too many professionals struggle with visible bots disrupting client meetings and cloud-based tools that couldn't meet privacy requirements. Frequently Asked Questions
What is the main difference between Meetily and Fireflies.ai?

The main difference is bot visibility and data processing approach. Fireflies joins meetings as a visible bot ('Fireflies Notetaker'), uploads audio to cloud servers for processing, and stores transcripts in the cloud. Meetily is bot-free (invisible to participants), transcribes locally on your device, and gives you control over how summaries are generated (local models or your own API key). Meetily Pro is $10/user/month billed annually, and Meetily also offers a free open-source Community Edition.

Can Meetily auto-join my calendar meetings like Fireflies?

Yes! Meetily Pro includes automatic meeting detection and calendar integration. The app uses hardware-level audio detection to automatically prompt you to start recording when a meeting begins. The Community Edition requires manual start/stop via the user interface or keyboard shortcuts.

Does Meetily have a mobile app like Fireflies?

No, Meetily is currently desktop-only (Windows and macOS). Mobile apps are planned for future release. If you need mobile access now, Fireflies is the better choice. However, Meetily's desktop app offers superior privacy with local processing and bot-free recording.

Is Meetily's transcription as accurate as Fireflies?

Yes, Meetily delivers excellent transcription accuracy across 99+ languages using state-of-the-art AI models (Whisper and Parakeet engines). Both tools use advanced AI for transcription, and in real-world use, the quality is virtually identical. The key difference: Meetily processes everything locally on your device, while Fireflies uploads to the cloud.

How does Meetily record meetings without a bot?

Meetily captures system-level audio directly from your computer. When you join a meeting with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, or any other platform, Meetily records the audio output from your system and microphone input. This happens entirely on your device without joining as a meeting participant, so other attendees never see a bot. Recording and transcription happen locally. For AI summaries, you choose your provider.

Can I use Meetily for team collaboration like Fireflies?

Yes, but it depends on the tier. The Community Edition (free and open source) is local-only. For team collaboration, Meetily offers Pro and Enterprise plans with centralized data management, admin dashboards, and shared transcript access across the team-while still maintaining local processing and privacy-first architecture.

Does Meetily integrate with CRM tools like Salesforce or HubSpot?

Not natively. Meetily Pro gives you the building blocks: signed webhooks when a summary is ready, and a built-in command-line tool and local API that export any meeting as Markdown, text or JSON, so a short script of your own can send notes to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. However, Fireflies offers more native integrations out-of-the-box (90+ apps). Since the Community Edition is open source, you can also build custom integrations for your specific workflow.

What are the cost differences between Meetily and Fireflies?

Meetily Pro is $10/user/month billed annually ($120/year). Fireflies Pro starts at a comparable rate. Meetily also offers a completely free Community Edition (open source, core features included) and custom pricing for Enterprise deployments. Fireflies requires a subscription for all users, with pricing ranging from $10-39/month depending on the plan. For teams of 20+ users, Meetily's ROI is typically achieved within 3-6 months.

Is Meetily HIPAA and GDPR compliant like Fireflies?

Yes, and Meetily's compliance approach is different. Fireflies requires an Enterprise plan ($39/month) with a signed BAA for HIPAA compliance, and GDPR compliance depends on third-party cloud processors. Meetily is compliant by design: transcription runs locally, recordings stay on your device, and you choose how summaries are processed (local models for regulated data, or cloud options for non-sensitive meetings). The open-source code allows security audits. For HIPAA use cases, use fully local summarization.

Can I record Discord, Slack huddles, or non-standard meeting platforms?

Yes! Meetily captures system audio, so it works with any platform that outputs audio through your computer: Discord, Slack huddles, WhatsApp calls, phone calls routed through desktop, podcasts, webinars, and even in-person meetings where audio is routed through your computer. Fireflies only works with integrated platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Webex.

Does Meetily work offline?

Yes, Meetily can work completely offline. Once installed, the transcription models run locally on your device without requiring internet connectivity. AI summaries can also run offline if you use local AI models like Llama or Mistral through Ollama. Fireflies requires internet access for all functionality since all processing happens in the cloud.

How do I switch from Fireflies to Meetily?

Switching is straightforward: 1) Export your transcripts from Fireflies (TXT, PDF, or DOCX format), 2) Download and install Meetily from https://meetily.ai/downloads/, 3) Configure your audio sources and choose a transcription engine (Whisper or Parakeet), 4) Join your next meeting and start recording. Many users run both tools initially-using Fireflies for team meetings (leveraging integrations) and Meetily for sensitive client meetings (privacy and bot-free).

What is the main difference between Meetily and Fireflies.ai?

The main difference is bot visibility and data processing approach. Fireflies joins meetings as a visible bot ('Fireflies Notetaker'), uploads audio to cloud servers for processing, and stores transcripts in the cloud. Meetily is bot-free (invisible to participants), transcribes locally on your device, and gives you control over how summaries are generated (local models or your own API key). Meetily Pro is $10/user/month billed annually, and Meetily also offers a free open-source Community Edition.

Can Meetily auto-join my calendar meetings like Fireflies?

Yes! Meetily Pro includes automatic meeting detection and calendar integration. The app uses hardware-level audio detection to automatically prompt you to start recording when a meeting begins. The Community Edition requires manual start/stop via the user interface or keyboard shortcuts.

Does Meetily have a mobile app like Fireflies?

No, Meetily is currently desktop-only (Windows and macOS). Mobile apps are planned for future release. If you need mobile access now, Fireflies is the better choice. However, Meetily's desktop app offers superior privacy with local processing and bot-free recording.

Is Meetily's transcription as accurate as Fireflies?

The key difference: Meetily processes everything locally on your device, while Fireflies uploads to the cloud.

How does Meetily record meetings without a bot?

Meetily captures system-level audio directly from your computer. When you join a meeting with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, or any other platform, Meetily records the audio output from your system and microphone input. This happens entirely on your device without joining as a meeting participant, so other attendees never see a bot. Recording and transcription happen locally. For AI summaries, you choose your provider.

Can I use Meetily for team collaboration like Fireflies?

Yes, but it depends on the tier. The Community Edition (free and open source) is local-only. For team collaboration, Meetily offers Pro and Enterprise plans with centralized data management, admin dashboards, and shared transcript access across the team-while still maintaining local processing and privacy-first architecture.

Does Meetily integrate with CRM tools like Salesforce or HubSpot?

Not natively. Meetily Pro gives you the building blocks: signed webhooks when a summary is ready, and a built-in command-line tool and local API that export any meeting as Markdown, text or JSON, so a short script of your own can send notes to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. What are the cost differences between Meetily and Fireflies?

Meetily Pro is $10/user/month billed annually ($120/year). Fireflies Pro starts at a comparable rate. Meetily also offers a completely free Community Edition (open source, core features included) and custom pricing for Enterprise deployments. Fireflies requires a subscription for all users, with pricing ranging from $10-39/month depending on the plan. For teams of 20+ users, Meetily's ROI is typically achieved within 3-6 months.

Is Meetily HIPAA and GDPR compliant like Fireflies?

Yes, and Meetily's compliance approach is different. Fireflies requires an Enterprise plan ($39/month) with a signed BAA for HIPAA compliance, and GDPR compliance depends on third-party cloud processors. Meetily is compliant by design: transcription runs locally, recordings stay on your device, and you choose how summaries are processed (local models for regulated data, or cloud options for non-sensitive meetings). The open-source code allows security audits. For HIPAA use cases, use fully local summarization.

Can I record Discord, Slack huddles, or non-standard meeting platforms?

Yes! Meetily captures system audio, so it works with any platform that outputs audio through your computer: Discord, Slack huddles, WhatsApp calls, phone calls routed through desktop, podcasts, webinars, and even in-person meetings where audio is routed through your computer. Fireflies only works with integrated platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Webex.

Yes, Meetily can work completely offline. Once installed, the transcription models run locally on your device without requiring internet connectivity. AI summaries can also run offline if you use local AI models like Llama or Mistral through Ollama. Fireflies requires internet access for all functionality since all processing happens in the cloud.

Switching is straightforward: 1) Export your transcripts from Fireflies (TXT, PDF, or DOCX format), 2) Download and install Meetily from https://meetily.ai/downloads/, 3) Configure your audio sources and choose a transcription engine (Whisper or Parakeet), 4) Join your next meeting and start recording. Many users run both tools initially-using Fireflies for team meetings (leveraging integrations) and Meetily for sensitive client meetings (privacy and bot-free).

The Problem with Cloud-Based Meeting Transcription

Before diving into the comparison, let's understand why enterprises are reconsidering cloud-based tools like Otter.ai.

Data Sovereignty Violations

When you use Otter.ai, every word spoken in your meetings is:

Recorded and uploaded to Otter.ai's servers (US-based)
Processed by their AI models (shared infrastructure)
Stored on their cloud platform (retention policies you don't control)
Potentially used for model training (unless you have enterprise plan with data processing agreements)

For EU companies, this creates GDPR Article 44 violations-cross-border data transfers to the US without adequate safeguards. The Schrems II ruling invalidated Privacy Shield, making US-based cloud processors legally problematic for European data.

The "Bot Problem"

Otter.ai joins your meetings as a visible bot participant-"Otter Assistant" appears in your Zoom, Teams, or Google Meet participant list. This creates:

Deal-killing moments: Prospects see the bot and question your data handling practices
Client discomfort: Sensitive discussions become guarded when participants see external recording
Compliance concerns: Healthcare providers can't have third-party bots in patient consultations
Professional image issues: Enterprise buyers expect discretion, not visible recording services

Feature-by-Feature Comparison: Meetily vs Otter.ai
Transcription Accuracy & Performance
Feature	Meetily	Otter.ai
Accuracy	Varies by model (Whisper models achieve competitive accuracy)	High accuracy (proprietary model)
Engines	Dual: Whisper + Parakeet	Single proprietary model
Whisper Engine	State-of-the-art open-source (Large v3)	N/A
Parakeet Engine	NVIDIA NeMo-based, optimized for speed	N/A
Languages	99+ languages	English + 20 languages (limited support)
Model Options	6 models across 2 engines	Single proprietary model
Custom Training	✅ Fine-tune on domain terminology	❌ No custom training
Offline Capability	✅ Works completely offline	❌ Requires internet connection

Winner: Meetily - Comparable accuracy with significantly more flexibility, dual engine choice, and offline support.

Privacy & Data Control

Data Location	Your device (local storage)	Otter.ai cloud servers (US)
Data Sovereignty	✅ Complete control	❌ Data leaves your control
GDPR Compliance	✅ Built-in (data never leaves EU if you're in EU)	⚠️ Requires DPA, Privacy Shield concerns
HIPAA Compliance	✅ Local-only = no BAA needed	⚠️ Requires BAA, still third-party risk
Encryption	✅ Your device encryption	⚠️ Encrypted but vendor-controlled
Data Retention	✅ You control 100%	⚠️ Vendor retention policies apply
Third-Party Access	❌ None (fully local)	⚠️ Otter.ai employees can access
Audit Capability	✅ Open source = full audit	❌ Proprietary black box

Winner: Meetily - Unquestionably superior for privacy and compliance requirements.

Meeting Experience & Usability
Feature	Meetily	Otter.ai
Bot Visibility	❌ Invisible (bot-free recording)	✅ Visible "Otter Assistant" joins
Participant Comfort	✅ No disruption or discomfort	⚠️ Participants see bot, may object
Platform Support	✅ All platforms (Zoom, Teams, Meet, Discord, any)	⚠️ Integrated platforms only
Setup Complexity	Medium (one-time desktop install)	Easy (browser-based)
Real-Time Transcription	✅ Yes (with sufficient hardware)	✅ Yes
Speaker Identification	✅ AI-powered diarization	✅ AI-powered diarization
Mobile Apps	❌ Desktop only (Windows/macOS)	✅ iOS and Android apps

Winner: Tie - Meetily excels at discretion and privacy; Otter.ai excels at ease-of-use and mobile access.

AI Features & Intelligence
Feature	Meetily	Otter.ai
AI Summaries	✅ Local LLM or API (user choice)	✅ Built-in AI summaries
Action Items	✅ Automatic extraction	✅ Automatic extraction
Topic Segmentation	✅ Yes	✅ Yes
Searchable Archive	✅ Yes (local search)	✅ Yes (cloud-based)
Custom AI Prompts	✅ Full customization (Ollama/Claude/GPT)	❌ Limited customization
Sentiment Analysis	✅ Via custom models	⚠️ Limited
Export Formats	Markdown (more coming)	TXT, PDF, DOCX, SRT

Winner: Split - Meetily offers more AI flexibility; Otter.ai has more export formats currently.

Pricing & Total Cost of Ownership
Pricing Model	Meetily	Otter.ai
Free Tier	✅ Full-featured Community Edition (MIT license)	⚠️ Limited (600 min/month, 30 min/meeting max)
Per-User Cost (Monthly)	$0 (Community) / $10/user/mo annual (Pro) / Custom (Enterprise)	$8.33/user/mo annual (regular $16.99)
Team (10 users)	Free Community or Pro ($10/user/month billed annually)	$1,000/year minimum
Team (100 users, 5 years)	Custom (one-time + support)	$50,000+ over 5 years
Hidden Costs	None for individual tier	Per-user scaling costs
Payment Model	Free (individual), custom (teams)	Recurring monthly subscription

Winner: Meetily - Dramatically lower TCO for individual users and teams.

When to Choose Meetily

Meetily is particularly well-suited for:

Healthcare providers: Need HIPAA-compliant transcription without third-party Business Associate Agreements
European companies: Require GDPR compliance with data residency in the EU
Financial services: Handle confidential M&A, legal, or strategic discussions
Government and defense: Work in air-gapped or classified environments
Privacy-conscious professionals: Want meeting intelligence without cloud dependency
Sales teams: Need invisible recording that doesn't alert prospects or clients

Step 1: Export Your Data from Otter.ai
Log into Otter.ai web dashboard
Navigate to each conversation
Click "Export" → Choose "TXT" or "PDF" format
Download all transcripts (Note: Otter.ai doesn't offer bulk export for free users)
Save audio recordings if you have access

Note: Otter.ai's export is conversation-by-conversation, which can be time-consuming for large archives.

Step 2: Install Meetily
macOS:

Download the .dmg installer from the Meetily Downloads page, open it, and drag Meetily to your Applications folder.

Windows:
Download meetily_x64-setup.exe from the Meetily Downloads page
Run the installer

Step 3: Configure Meetily
Launch Meetily from Applications (Mac) or Start Menu (Windows)
Select Transcription Engine:

Want to take control of your meeting transcriptions with 100% privacy? This comprehensive guide will walk you through installing Meetily-a free, open-source AI meeting assistant that processes everything locally on your device.

Prerequisites
Windows 10/11, or macOS 11.0+ (Big Sur or later) on an Apple Silicon Mac
8GB+ RAM (16GB recommended)
10GB free storage space
Internet connection (for initial download only)

Why Choose Meetily?

Before we dive into installation, here's what makes Meetily special:

Privacy First: Transcription runs locally on your device. For summaries, choose local AI or your own API key
Free & Open Source: MIT licensed Community Edition, free
Bot-Free: Invisible to meeting participants (no "Meetily Bot" joining calls)
Works Offline: Internet only needed for initial setup
Platform-Agnostic: Works with Zoom, Teams, Meet, Discord, any meeting software
31,094+ GitHub Stars: Trusted by privacy-conscious developers worldwide

Part 1: Installation
Option A: Install on macOS
Method 1: Download from Website (Easiest)

The simplest way to install Meetily is directly from our website.

Step 1: Visit Downloads Page

Go to meetily.ai/downloads
Select macOS from the platform selector
Choose between Community (free) or Pro version
Click "Download for macOS"

Step 2: Install Application

Open the downloaded .dmg file
Drag Meetily icon to Applications folder
Eject the installer disk image

Step 3: Launch Meetily

Open Applications folder
Double-click Meetily
If security warning appears, right-click → "Open" → Confirm
Troubleshooting macOS Security:

If macOS blocks Meetily with "App cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified":

xattr -c /Applications/Meetily.app

Then try opening again. This removes the quarantine flag from the downloaded app.

Method 2: GitHub Releases (For More Control)

For developers who want to verify releases, check changelogs, or download specific versions:

Step 1: Download Installer

Visit Meetily GitHub Releases
Look for the macOS .dmg file in the latest release
Download and unzip if needed

Step 2: Install Application

Follow the same installation steps as Method 1 above.

Option B: Install on Windows
Method 1: Download from Website (Easiest)

The simplest way to install Meetily is directly from our website.

Step 1: Visit Downloads Page

Go to meetily.ai/downloads
Select Windows from the platform selector
Choose between Community (free) or Pro version
Click "Download for Windows"
Save the .exe installer to Downloads folder

Step 2: Prepare for Installation

Before running the installer:

Right-click the downloaded .exe file
Select "Properties"
Check "Unblock" checkbox (if present)
Click "OK"

Step 3: Run Installer

Double-click the installer file
If Windows Defender SmartScreen appears:
Click "More info"
Click "Run anyway"
Follow installation wizard:
Accept license agreement
Choose installation directory (default recommended)
Create desktop shortcut (optional)
Click "Install"

Step 4: Launch Meetily

Click "Finish" in installer
Meetily launches automatically
Or: Find in Start Menu → "Meetily"
Troubleshooting Windows Defender:

Windows Defender may flag new releases. This is normal for open-source software without code signing certificates. You can:

Click "More info" → "Run anyway" (safe for official releases)
Add exception in Windows Defender if needed
Verify download hash matches official release (for extra security)
Method 2: GitHub Releases (For More Control)

For developers who want to verify releases, check changelogs, or download specific versions:

Step 1: Download Installer

Visit Meetily GitHub Releases
Download the Windows .exe installer from the latest release
Save to Downloads folder

Step 2: Install Application

Follow the same installation steps as Method 1 above.

Option C: Build from Source (Advanced Users)

For developers who want to customize Meetily:

Prerequisites:
Rust toolchain (rustup)
Node.js 18+
Python 3.10+
Git

Important: Read the build guide first

Before building, read the comprehensive Building Guide for detailed instructions.

Quick Build Steps:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/Zackriya-Solutions/meetily.git
cd meetily/frontend

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Development builds
npm run tauri:dev          # GPU accelerated build (recommended)
npm run tauri dev          # CPU-only build

# Production builds
npm run tauri:build        # or
npm run tauri build

For detailed troubleshooting and platform-specific instructions, see the Building Guide.

Part 2: Initial Configuration

Once Meetily launches, you'll see the setup wizard.

Step 1: Welcome & System Check

The wizard verifies:

✅ Sufficient disk space (10GB+)
✅ Memory requirements (8GB+ RAM)
✅ Audio permissions granted
✅ FFmpeg availability (installed automatically if missing)

Click "Next" when all checks pass.

Step 2: Choose Transcription Engine & Model

Meetily offers two transcription engines-a unique feature no other open-source meeting assistant has:

Option 1: Parakeet Engine (Default, Recommended)

Parakeet is selected by default and provides the best balance of speed and accuracy for most users.

Best For: Real-time transcription with excellent accuracy
Performance: Optimized for fast transcription on modern hardware
Memory: Efficient with Int8 quantization (~1-3GB RAM)
Processing: Significantly faster than Whisper with lower resource usage
Available Parakeet Models:
Lightning (Recommended): Best balance of accuracy and speed for most users
Light: Lighter model for older hardware
Compact: Most compact option with minimal resource usage
Option 2: Whisper Engine (For Maximum Accuracy)

For users who need the highest accuracy and multilingual support.

Best For: Maximum accuracy, broad language support (99+ languages)
Processing: Established, well-tested models
Access: Basic models available by default, advanced Whisper models (Medium, Large) accessible in Advanced Settings
Model	Size	RAM Usage	Speed	Best For
Tiny	~75MB	~1GB	Very Fast	Quick notes, testing
Base	~140MB	~1-2GB	Fast	Casual meetings
Small	~460MB	~2-3GB	Medium	General use
Medium	~1.5GB	~4-5GB	Slower	High accuracy needed (Advanced Settings)
Large v3	~3GB	~8-10GB	Slowest	Professional/critical meetings (Advanced Settings)
Which Should You Choose?

Use Parakeet (Default) if:

You want the best overall experience (recommended for most users)
You need real-time transcription without lag
You want lower CPU usage and battery consumption
You have any modern hardware from the last 5 years

Switch to Whisper if:

You need maximum accuracy for medical, legal, or critical meetings
You require 99+ language support
You have powerful hardware and can afford slower processing
You need specific language optimizations

Default Setup:

Meetily uses Parakeet Lightning by default, which provides excellent accuracy and the fastest transcription speed.

Model Download:
After selecting your preferred engine and model, you'll be prompted to download it
Click "Download Model" to begin the one-time download
The model downloads to your local storage (no internet needed afterward)
You can change models later in Settings if needed
Step 3: Configure Audio Sources
Microphone Selection:
Click "Microphone" dropdown
Select your input device:
Built-in Microphone (laptops)
External USB microphone
Headset microphone
Test: Speak and watch the level meter
System Audio Capture:

This captures audio from your meeting platform (Zoom, Teams, etc.).

macOS:

Meetily uses BlackHole or similar virtual audio device
If not installed: Click "Install Audio Driver"
Follow prompts to install virtual audio device
Restart Meetily after installation

Windows:

Meetily uses Windows WASAPI (built-in)
Click "Enable System Audio"
Grant permissions if prompted
No additional software needed
Test Audio Capture:
Play a YouTube video or music
Check "System Audio" level meter
Verify both microphone and system audio show levels
Step 4: Storage Location

Choose where Meetily saves your transcripts and recordings.

Setting Storage Location:
The storage location is accessible and configurable directly from the Meetily UI
Access it from Settings or from the meeting details page
Click "Change" or "Browse" to select your preferred folder
Choose cloud-synced folder (Dropbox, OneDrive) for automatic backup
Or external drive for extra privacy
What Gets Stored:

Your recordings are saved in the meetily-recordings folder with the following files:

transcript.md - Full meeting transcript
summary.md - AI-generated summary (if enabled)
audio.mp3 - Audio recording (optional)

You can view and change your storage location anytime from Settings or access individual meeting files from the meeting details page.

Step 5: AI Summarization (Optional)

Meetily can generate AI summaries after each meeting. This step is completely optional-transcription works without AI summaries.

Option 1: Local LLM with Ollama (Recommended for Privacy)

Step 1: Install Ollama

Visit ollama.ai and download for your platform
Install Ollama following their instructions
Verify installation: Open terminal and run ollama --version

Step 2: Download a Model

# Recommended lightweight model (800MB)
ollama pull gemma2:2b

# Or for better quality (4.7GB)
ollama pull llama3.2:latest

Step 3: Start Ollama Server

ollama serve

Keep this terminal window open while using Meetily. The server runs at http://localhost:11434

Step 4: Configure in Meetily

Open Meetily → Settings → Model Settings
Select provider: Ollama
Enter model name (e.g., gemma2:2b or llama3.2:latest)
(Optional) Custom endpoint if not using default
Option 2: API-Based LLMs

If you prefer cloud LLMs, Meetily supports:

Anthropic Claude: Settings → Model Settings → Provider: Claude → Enter API key
OpenAI GPT: Settings → Model Settings → Provider: OpenAI → Enter API key
Groq: Settings → Model Settings → Provider: Groq → Enter API key (free tier available)
OpenRouter: Settings → Model Settings → Provider: OpenRouter → Enter API key

Note: Using API-based LLMs means your meeting transcripts are sent to third-party servers for summarization.

Option 3: Skip for Now
You can enable AI summaries later in Settings → Model Settings
Transcription works perfectly without AI summaries
Manual review of transcripts works fine initially

Click "Finish" to complete setup!

Part 3: Recording Your First Meeting
Before the Meeting
1. Launch Meetily
Open from Applications (Mac) or Start Menu (Windows)
Ensure it's running (icon in menu bar/system tray)
2. Join Your Meeting
Open Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, Discord, etc.
Join meeting as normal
No special setup needed per platform
3. Start Recording

Community Edition:

In Meetily, click "Record" button to start recording

Pro Edition:

Automatic Meeting Detection: Pro users benefit from automatic meeting detection
Meetily automatically detects when you join a meeting and can start recording
Global Shortcuts: Use Option+X (Mac) / Alt+X (Win) to start/stop recording from anywhere without UI interaction
Floating Recording Panel: Access recording controls via a convenient floating panel
You can also manually start/stop recordings as needed
Configure auto-detection settings in Settings → Meeting Detection
During the Meeting
Real-Time Transcription Display:
Recording in progress...

Good morning everyone, let's start with our product updates.

Sure, I can begin. We've made great progress on the authentication feature...
Controls:
Pause: Temporarily pause recording (excludes segments from transcript)
Bookmark: Mark important moments (adds timestamp marker)
Stop: End recording (triggers AI summary)
Performance Monitoring:
CPU usage indicator
Memory usage
Transcription lag (should be <2 seconds)
After the Meeting
1. Stop Recording
Click "Stop" button in Meetily
Pro users can use global shortcut: Option+X (Mac) / Alt+X (Win)
2. AI Summary Generation (if enabled)
Processing summary...
- Analyzing transcript
- Extracting key points
- Identifying action items
- Detecting decisions

Summary complete! (takes 10-60 seconds)
3. Review & Export

Community Edition:

View transcript in Meetily
Export to Markdown
Copy to clipboard for pasting elsewhere

Pro Edition (Additional Features):

Audio Upload: Upload existing audio files for transcription
Templates: Use pre-built templates for different meeting types
Chat: Interactive chat with your transcripts using AI
Integrations: Connect with your favorite tools
Cloud Sync: Sync transcripts across devices
Sharable Links: Share transcripts with team members across organizations

Part 4: Platform-Specific Configuration
Google Meet

No special setup needed!

System audio capture works automatically
Just click "Record" in Meetily before/during meeting

Tips:

Use Chrome or Edge (better audio routing)
Ensure "Use original sound" is enabled in Meet settings
Zoom

Configuration:

Open Zoom → Settings → Audio
Enable "Original Sound for Musicians"
Disable "Suppress background noise" (optional, for better accuracy)

Recording:

Start Meetily recording BEFORE joining Zoom call
Or start after joining (may miss first few seconds)
Microsoft Teams

Configuration:

Open Teams → Settings → Devices
Test your microphone and speakers
Disable "Noise suppression" for better transcription accuracy

Note: Teams' noise suppression can filter out background speakers. Disable for meetings where you need to capture all participants.

Discord

Works perfectly with system audio capture!

No special configuration needed
Captures all voice channels
Real-time transcription during gaming sessions or community calls
Slack Huddles

Configuration:

Join Slack Huddle
Start Meetily recording
System audio captures Huddle audio automatically

Part 5: Advanced Configuration
GPU Acceleration (Automatic)

Meetily automatically detects and uses GPU acceleration if available on your system. No manual configuration needed!

How It Works:
GPU acceleration is detected and enabled automatically at application startup
On macOS: Uses Metal acceleration (built into Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3)
On Windows: Uses compatible NVIDIA CUDA or AMD ROCm if available
Fallback to CPU if no compatible GPU is found
Supported GPUs:
Apple Silicon: M1, M2, M3, M4 (automatic Metal acceleration)
NVIDIA: GTX 1060 or newer (requires CUDA)
AMD: RX 580 or newer (requires ROCm on Linux)

Note: GPU acceleration provides 3-10x faster transcription compared to CPU-only processing. If you experience issues, the app will automatically fall back to CPU processing.

Global Shortcuts (Pro Only)

Pro users have access to global shortcuts that work without UI interaction:

Available Shortcuts:
Start/Stop Recording: Option+X (Mac) / Alt+X (Win)
Works from anywhere on your system, even when Meetily is minimized
No need to switch windows or interact with the UI
Perfect for seamless recording workflow

Configure and customize shortcuts in Settings → Shortcuts (Pro only)

Application Settings
Notification Preferences:
Settings → Preferences → Enable/disable recording notifications
Control which events trigger notifications
Respect Do Not Disturb mode
Storage Locations:
Settings → Preferences → View storage paths
Database location: Where meeting metadata is stored
Models directory: Where transcription models are cached
Recordings folder: Where audio and transcripts are saved
Analytics:
Settings → Preferences → Analytics consent toggle
Opt in/out of usage analytics
Helps improve the app without compromising privacy

Part 6: Troubleshooting Common Issues
Issue 1: "No Audio Detected"

Symptoms: Recording starts but no transcription appears

Solutions:

Check Audio Permissions:
macOS: System Preferences → Security → Microphone → Enable Meetily
Windows: Settings → Privacy → Microphone → Allow Meetily
Test Audio Sources:
Settings → Audio → Test Microphone
Speak and verify level meter moves
Restart Audio Devices:
Unplug and replug headset/microphone
Restart Meetily
Issue 2: "Transcription Too Slow"

Symptoms: Real-time transcription lags 10+ seconds behind speech

Solutions:

Use Smaller Model:
Switch from Large → Medium or Small
Settings → Models → Select smaller model
Enable GPU:
Settings → Performance → Enable GPU
Requires compatible graphics card
Close Other Apps:
Free up RAM and CPU
Close Chrome tabs, video editors, etc.
Issue 3: "Model Download Fails"

Symptoms: Whisper model download stuck or fails

Solutions:

Check Internet Connection:
Ensure stable internet
Large v3 is 3GB download (takes time)
Manual Download:
Download from Hugging Face
Settings → Models → "Import Model" → Select file
Clear Cache:
Settings → Advanced → "Clear Model Cache"
Retry download
Issue 4: "Meetily Won't Launch"

Symptoms: Double-clicking icon does nothing

macOS Solutions:

# Check if app is blocked
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Meetily.app

# Check for errors
/Applications/Meetily.app/Contents/MacOS/Meetily

Windows Solutions:

Run as Administrator: Right-click Meetily → "Run as administrator"
Check Event Viewer: Windows → Event Viewer → Application logs (Look for Meetily errors)
Reinstall: Uninstall via Control Panel, download fresh installer, install again
Issue 5: "Poor Transcription Accuracy"

Symptoms: Many words transcribed incorrectly

Solutions:

Upgrade Whisper Model:
Base → Small or Medium
Accuracy improves significantly
Improve Audio Quality:
Use external microphone (not laptop built-in)
Reduce background noise
Move closer to microphone
Disable Noise Suppression:
In Zoom/Teams settings
Noise suppression can confuse Whisper

Managed deployment by Zackriya team
Extended support

Congratulations! You now have Meetily installed and configured. You're ready to:

✅ Record meetings with complete privacy
✅ Get accurate AI transcriptions
✅ Generate automatic summaries

Get started:

Click "Record" in Meetily
Review transcript and summary after
Enjoy privacy-first meeting intelligence!

About the Author

Written by the Meetily team. We built Meetily to provide professionals with privacy-first meeting intelligence that doesn't compromise on features or usability. Our mission is to make AI meeting transcription accessible to everyone while keeping your data completely private.
